title: Music Theory Basics
subtitle: 3-week starter course · no instrument needed
description: Read notes and rhythms, build major scales and key signatures, name intervals, spell chords and hear how progressions and cadences work.

labels.projectsIntro: Apply what you learned to real music you like. Each counts as done when its written answers are in.

phases.title: Phase 1 · Reading music
phases.goal: Name notes on both clefs and count rhythms in simple and compound time.

phases.title: Phase 2 · Harmony
phases.goal: Build major scales, name intervals, spell the chords of a key and recognise cadences. Pass the final checkpoint with 70% or more.

weeks.title: Notes and rhythm
weeks.goal: Read notes in treble and bass clef, use sharps and flats, and count note values in 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 and 6/8.

tasks.title: Pitch, note names and the staff
tasks.desc: Letter names, octaves, half and whole steps, sharps and flats, and the two clefs.

tasks.title: Note values, rests and time signatures
tasks.desc: How long each note lasts, dots and ties, and simple vs compound time.

tasks.title: Daily reviews and the weekly self-check
tasks.desc: Open Today on most days: recall cards and drill reviews first, then the new lesson. Finish the week with the self-check quiz.

tasks.title: Find middle C on a keyboard
tasks.desc: Open any piano app or a real keyboard. Find every C, then middle C (C4), then play C up to the next C on white keys only.

crit.label: I found middle C and played the C major scale

quiz.q: Which white-key pairs are a half step apart?
quiz.why: There is no black key between E and F or between B and C.

quiz.q: The bottom line of the treble clef is:
quiz.why: Treble lines are E G B D F.
Two beats, each a dotted quarter split into three.

weeks.title: Scales and intervals
weeks.goal: Spell any major scale, read key signatures, and name intervals by number and quality.

tasks.title: Major scales and key signatures
tasks.desc: The W W H W W W H pattern, the spelling rule, and the orders of sharps and flats.

tasks.title: Intervals: number and quality
tasks.desc: Count letters, then compare with the lower note's major scale.

tasks.title: Project 1: the key of a song
tasks.desc: Pick a song you like and find its sheet music or chords online. Find its key signature (or work out the key from the chords), spell that major scale, and name three intervals from the first line of the melody.

crit.label: Song, key, and its major scale spelled out
Three intervals from the melody, each with how you named it

tasks.title: Daily reviews and the weekly self-check
tasks.desc: Open Today on most days: recall cards and drill reviews first, then the new lesson. Finish the week with the self-check quiz.

quiz.q: What is the major scale pattern?
o: W H W W H W W
W W H W W W H
W W W H W W H
H W W W W H W
quiz.why: Half steps fall between degrees 3–4 and 7–8.

quiz.q: Two sharps in a key signature are:
quiz.why: Sharps always come in the order F C G D A E B, so two sharps are F♯ and C♯: the key of D major.

quiz.q: C up to E♭ is a:
quiz.why: Three letters (a third), a half step smaller than C–E, so minor.

quiz.q: How many half steps in a perfect fourth?

weeks.title: Chords and progressions
weeks.goal: Spell triads of every quality, use Roman numerals, and recognise the four cadences. Pass the final checkpoint.

tasks.title: Triads and the chords of a key
tasks.desc: Four triad qualities, I ii iii IV V vi vii°, inversions and V7.

tasks.title: Chord progressions and cadences
tasks.desc: Chord functions, common progressions and how phrases end.

tasks.title: Project 2: analyse a progression
tasks.desc: Take the chords of a song you like (any chord site works). Write them out, convert them to Roman numerals in the song's key, mark the tonic, predominant and dominant chords, and find at least one cadence.

crit.label: The chords and their Roman numerals
Functions and the cadence you found, with the chords that make it

tasks.title: Final checkpoint (30 minutes)
tasks.desc: A timed mix of exercises and drills from all three weeks. Retake as often as you like; the best score counts.

tasks.title: Daily reviews and the weekly self-check
tasks.desc: Open Today on most days: recall cards and drill reviews first, then the new lesson. Finish the week with the self-check quiz.

quiz.q: A minor triad is built from:
quiz.why: Minor third at the bottom, major third on top; the outer interval is a perfect fifth.

quiz.q: In a major key, ii is:
quiz.why: I ii iii IV V vi vii°: lower case is minor.
The ear expects I and hears vi instead.
A major: degree 4 is D and degree 5 is E.
